translations.text: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Dai, and David’s mighty warriors did not follow Adonijah.
Go up after him, and let him come and sit on my throne. He will reign after me. I have appointed him to be king over Israel and Judah.
He said to her, “Speak to King Solomon, for he will not refuse you, and ask him to give me Abishag the Shilomite as my wife.”

Benaiah went into the tent of the LORD and said to him, “This is what the king says: ‘Come out.’” He said, “I will not come out. I will die here.” Benaiah reported this to the king, saying, “This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me.”
After three years, two of Shimei’s servants fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. They told Shimei, “Look, your servants are in Gath.”
Why did you not keep the oath sworn to the LORD and the command I gave you?
The LORD said to Solomon, “Because you asked for this, and did not ask for wealth for yourself, or for the lives of your enemies, or for many days for yourself, but asked for wisdom to hear cases,”
Abinshar was in charge of the royal household, and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the tribute.
Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying:
Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, “I have heard the message you sent me. I will fulfill all your wishes concerning cedar wood and cypress wood.”
The house, the inner temple, was forty cubits long.

His own house, where he lived, was in another courtyard, farther inside than the porch, and he built it in the same style. He also built a house in the same style for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Solomon had married.
It was constructed of fine stones and large stones, stones measuring ten cubits and stones measuring eight cubits.
He made ten bronze basins. Each basin held forty measures and measured four cubits. There was one basin on each stand, and so it was for all ten stands.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
Turn toward your servant’s prayer and his plea, LORD my God, and listen to the plea and prayer that your servant offers before you today.
So that they may fear you all the days they live on the land you gave to their ancestors.
Hear their prayer and their plea from heaven, and uphold their cause.

They will say, “Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of the land of Egypt, and embraced the gods of other nations, served them, and worshiped them. That is why the LORD brought all this disaster upon them.”
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of refined gold. He applied six hundred minas of gold to each large shield.
He also made three hundred shields of refined gold. He applied three hundred minas of gold to each shield, and the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
All the kings of the earth sought to see Solomon and hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the idol of Moab, on the mountain opposite Jerusalem, and for Milcom, the idol of the Ammonites.
For Joab stayed there for six months, with all Israel alongside him, until he had killed every male in Edom.

The king did not listen to the people, for the provocation came from the LORD, so that the LORD might fulfill the words he had spoken through his servant Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.
He built a house of high places and appointed priests from among the people who were not descendants of Levi.
Go and tell Jeroboam, ‘This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel.’
But you have done more evil than all who were before you. You went and made cast-metal gods for yourself to provoke me to anger, and you cast me behind your back.
There was also prostitution in the land, and they practiced all the abominations of the nations that the Lord had destroyed before the Israelites.
He followed all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not wholly devoted to the Lord his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
The rest of Abijah’s deeds and everything he did are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
Asa did what was right before the Lord, as his father David had done.
He removed the prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols his ancestors had made.
The rest of Baasha’s deeds, everything he did, and all his might are recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
The people who followed Omri proved stronger than the people who followed Tibni. Tibni died, and Omri became king.
He stretched himself over the boy three times and called to the Lord, saying, ‘Lord my God, let this boy’s life return to him.’
When Jezebel was killing the prophets of God, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them in a cave, fifty men at a time, and supplied them with bread and water.
They divided the route between them to travel through it. Ahab went alone along one route, and Obadiah went alone along another route.

Have I not told my lord what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of God? I took a hundred men from among the Lord’s prophets and hid them in a cave, fifty men at a time, and supplied them with bread and water.
Elijah approached all the people and said, ‘How long will you be divided between two sides? If the Lord is God, follow him; and if Baal is, follow him.’ But the people gave him no answer.

At noon Elijah mocked them and said, ‘Call out loudly, for he is a god! Perhaps he is thinking, or perhaps he is attending to some business, or perhaps he is on a journey, or perhaps he is asleep and needs to wake up.’
While he was turning this way and that, the sky became covered with clouds and wind, and there was heavy rain. Ahab rode off and went to Jezreel.

He went a day’s journey into the wilderness and sat under a terebinth tree. He asked that he might die and said, ‘I have had enough now, Lord. Take my life from me, for I am no better than my ancestors.’
He turned and saw at his head [?] bread baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank, then lay down again.
Tomorrow at this time I will send my servants to you. They will search your houses and your servants’ houses, and they will take in their hands everything their eyes desire and bring it away.

Say to him, ‘This is what the Lord says: You have killed, and now you have taken possession! This is what the Lord says: In the place where dogs licked Naboth’s blood, dogs will also lick your own blood.’
He became utterly defiled and followed idols, as the Amorites had done, whom the Lord destroyed before the Israelites.
He said to Jehoshaphat, ‘Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead?’ Jehoshaphat said, ‘I will go as you do; my people are like your people, and my horses are like your horses.’
Micaiah said, ‘Therefore hear the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the army of heaven standing above him, on his right and on his left.’
